item.title: フーシ派、サウジ最大製油所攻撃と主張 軍用機標的とも表明
item.description: [ドバイ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ドバイ　２７日　ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２７日、サウジアラビア最大の石油精製施設であるラス・タヌラ製油所を弾道ミサイルで攻撃したと表明した。また、サウジ軍の軍用機を攻撃したほか、紅海の重要な海上輸送路であるバベルマンデブ海峡付近でサウジの支援を受ける部隊の前進を撃退したと表明した。

フーシ派のヤヒヤ・サリー報道官は、攻撃を受けラス・タヌラ製油所で火災が発生したとしている。サウジ当局は現時点で攻撃を確認していない。ブルームバーグ・ニュースは関係筋の話として、サウジ当局がラス・タヌラの石油積み出しターミナル付近で発生した火災を封じ込めたと報じた。

フーシ派はこのほか、ナジュラン空港に駐機していた軍用輸送機２機と、ハミスムシャイトの空軍基地を攻撃したと表明。サウジは現時点でこれらの攻撃を確認していない。

また、フーシ派と戦うサウジ主導の有志連合は、フーシ派がサウジの首都リヤドに向けて発射した弾道ミサイル２発を迎撃したと表明。午後にリヤドで一時、空襲警報が発令された。

ラス・タヌラ製油所はペルシャ湾岸に位置しており、処理能力は日量５５万バレル。石油積み出しターミナルも併設されている。サウジの石油輸出のほぼ全量はペルシャ湾岸のラス・タヌラと紅海沿岸のヤンブーという２つの主要港を経由。フーシ派はこれまでも両施設を攻撃している。

item.title: High inflation to persist globally into next year, Reuters poll shows
item.description: BENGALURU, Oct 27 : High inflation will persist in the global economy well into next year, according to hundreds of economists polled by Reuters, who are now increasingly concerned that price pressures will become entrenched beyond rising energy costs caused by the conflict in the Middle East.More than $1 tri

item.content:encoded:

High inflation to persist globally into next year, Reuters poll shows

FAST

BENGALURU, Oct 27 : High inflation will persist in the global economy well into next year, according to hundreds of economists polled by Reuters, who are now increasingly concerned that price pressures will become entrenched beyond rising energy costs caused by the conflict in the Middle East. More than $1 trillion of investment in artificial intelligence technology globally since last year has made some economies more resilient at a time when cost of living pressures are squeezing households and shaping national politics. Most central banks have raised interest rates only a few times or not at all, but more could come if inflation pressures broaden. A global rout in bond markets in recent months has also tightened financial conditions through higher yields. Crude oil prices, which have stayed above $100 a barrel since October 7, hit a six-month high of over $117 last week and are up more than 60 per cent since the US-Israeli war with Iran began almost eight months ago.

Even forecasters who did not anticipate a quick end to the war are now sounding more concerned about inflation resurgence, particularly given the resilience of global growth. More than 500 economists Reuters surveyed globally this month raised their 2027 inflation forecasts for 31 of the 50 economies polled on and growth forecasts for 23 of them. "I am getting much more concerned about inflation again," said Janet Henry, global chief economist at HSBC. "The longer the situation evolves and escalates in the Middle East and the higher the broad basket of price pressures builds, the greater the likelihood that we get not just higher but more persistent inflation." Economists raised 2027 inflation forecasts for 15 of 21 developed economies covered. That suggests inflation worries are spreading and affecting economies that typically experience low price pressures. Cumulatively, median forecasts for 2027 inflation over the past three quarterly polls have risen by 0.7 per centage points for Britain, 0.5 per centage points for the euro zone and only 0.2 per centage points so far for the US. They have risen by 0.4 per centage points for India and by 0.5 per centage point for Brazil. "Higher energy prices continue to ripple through the global economy, but economic activity remains resilient, supported by the AI-led investment cycle and firmer-than-expected activity across several regions," Seth Carpenter, global chief economist at Morgan Stanley, said in a note. "The inflation picture has become more complex as signs of energy pass-through into core measures are beginning to emerge." The effects of rising prices on household budgets have taken centre stage in various political campaigns across the world. Opinion polls show voters ahead of US midterm elections on November 3 are preoccupied with these issues and Brazil's presidential election, which gave incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva his fourth non-consecutive term, was also fought on cost of living issues. In contrast to two previous polls in April and July, which painted a weak-growth, high-inflation scenario, the latest forecasts lean towards one where price pressures accompany more robust economic performance. Economists upgraded their global growth forecasts for both this year and next, to 3.0 per cent and 3.2 per cent, respectively, from 2.9 per cent and 3.1 per cent in the July poll, though the 2027 forecast is lower than the 3.4 per cent the International Monetary Fund is predicting. The US, which leads in AI capital expenditure that has now become the main driver of domestic growth, is forecast to expand 2.3 per cent this year and 2.1 per cent in 2027. (Other stories from the Reuters global economic poll)

Source: Reuters

item.title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as premium drinks, sodas hold strong
item.description: Coca-Cola has lifted its annual profit forecast, driven by robust demand for a range of beverages, particularly zero-sugar options. The company now anticipates earnings per share growth of at least 9% by 2026. Their third-quarter revenue soared to $13.38 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations, while Coca-Cola's strong showing stands in sharp contrast to PepsiCo's recent downgrades and cost-cutting plans. Following these promising results, Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its annual profit forecast, betting on resilient demand for its zero-sugar sodas and pricier beverages such as fairlife milk and sparkling soft drinks.The company now expects comparable currency-neutral earnings per share to grow at least 9% in 2026, up from its previous forecast of 7% to 8%.Coca-Cola's third-quarter revenue rose 7.4% to $13.38 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $12.92 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.As high food and fuel prices make consumers more selective, Coca-Cola has sought to sustain demand by offering smaller, cheaper packs while rolling out pricier new flavours such as Coca-Cola Cherry Float.The company also benefited from demand during the soccer World Cup in July, including a brief sales boost for its energy drink brands.Its performance contrasts with rival PepsiCo, which lowered its annual targets earlier this month and stepped up cost cuts as it grapples with weak demand for snacks in North America.Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading. The stock has jumped about 33% in 2026 and is on track for a third straight year of gains, despite broader weakness in consumer spending and market volatility stemming from the war in Iran.

item.title: オレシュキで局地停戦開始、ロ・ウ双方が発表 キーウなどでは攻撃継続
item.description:
Dan Peleschuk Anna Voitenko
[キーウ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Peleschuk　Anna Voitenko

[キーウ ２７日 ロイター] - ロシアとウクライナは２７日、ロシアが占領するウクライナ南部ヘルソン州オレシュキでの人道支援活動を可能にするため局地的な停戦を開始した。停戦により食料・医薬品不足が深刻なオレシュキへの支援物資搬入や住民の避難が可能になる。ただ、首都キーウなど他の地域では攻撃が続いている。

ロシアとウクライナはともに、前線に位置するオレシュ周辺での停戦を順守していると表明した。停戦はウクライナ時間午前３時（０１００ＧＭＴ、日本時間午前１０時）に発効し、１１月１日まで続く予定。

オレシュキは２０２２年２月からロシア占領下にあり、食料支援が滞るなどして住民の人道危機が深刻化。ホワイトハウスは先週、トランプ米大統領のメラニア夫人がオレシュキでの停戦実現に貢献したと発表した。

一方、キーウ市当局によると、２７日の新たな攻撃で市内の南橋と地下鉄インフラが被害を受けて通行や運行が停止、少なくとも１人が死亡した。

＜ロシアによる占領＞

オレシュキはウクライナ南部ヘルソン州のドニプロ川東岸に位置し、対岸にはウクライナ軍が支配するヘルソン市がある。ロシア軍は２２年２月の全面侵攻開始直後に制圧、支配を続けている。オレシュキは戦争での広範な被害のほか、２３年に付近のカホフカダムが破壊された際には、洪水でも甚大な被害を受けた。

米国によると、戦前２万４０００人だった人口は、現在わずか数千人に減っている。住民や当局者は、食料や医薬品、その他の生活必需品が深刻に不足していると報告。水道や電気、ガス、地域暖房の供給もほぼ途絶えている。食料や水を手に入れるだけのために住民は地雷が散在する道路を移動している状況だ。

ウクライナとロシアの当局者は、支援物資の搬入と住民の移動を可能にする人道回廊を設置すると表明。道路の地雷除去が必要になるとみられ、数日かかる可能性がある。

ウクライナとロシアは、オレシュキの人道危機の責任を互いに非難している。民間人にとって最大の脅威はドローンで、同市は両軍の無人機が容易に到達できる範囲にある。

＜キーウに新たな攻撃＞

ロシアによる夜間の攻撃ではキーウの重要な橋である南橋が被害を受けた。ゼレンスキー氏は、ウクライナの物流網に対する「攻撃の深刻な激化」だと述べた。ウクライナ軍関係者によると、南橋には弾道ミサイル「イスカンデル」４発が命中した。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、ほかの１０地域でも夜間にエネルギー施設や物流拠点、インフラが攻撃された。

ロシア国防省は、軍事目標を狙った攻撃で、キーウの交通インフラ、ハルキウ州の物流拠点のほか、産業施設や貨物船を攻撃したと発表した。

ロシアでは、ウクライナとの国境に近い西部ブリャンスク市でドローン攻撃により１人が死亡したと当局が発表した。ウクライナのザポリージャ州のロシア支配地域ではバスが攻撃され、当局者によると１人が死亡、３０人が負傷した。

item.title: Lula's win in Brazil deals harsh blow to Trump’s ‘Donroe Doctrine’: McGeever
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise reelection victory on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s Donroe Doctrine, a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"surprise reelection victory"] on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s [USN:L1N43A0RG TEXT:""Donroe Doctrine,""] a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing. Trump's grand plans at the start of the year to solidify Washington's influence over Latin America were epitomized by US forces' extraordinary [USN:L6N3Y407K TEXT:"capture and extradition"] of Venezuela's leftist President Nicolas Maduro on January 3. Lula's victory has thrown a spanner in the works. South America's most populous nation will be led for another four years by the [USN:L6N46B06R TEXT:"veteran leftist"] and long-standing critic of US influence. Trump [USN:L6N46C02Y TEXT:"said on Monday"] that he likes Lula and gets along well with him, but it's safe to say he would have had a more cordial relationship with Lula’s right-wing opponent, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. What makes Lula's win even more vexing for Washington is that it is likely to strengthen Brazil's ties with China, a process that Lula has long championed. China overtook the US as Brazil's largest trading partner in 2009. Officially, Lula will avoid aligning himself too closely with either superpower. "We are no one's backyard!" Lula told thousands of supporters at his victory rally in Sao Paulo on Sunday. That could be interpreted as a warning to the US and China that Brazil will not be bullied into relinquishing control of its vast resources, from energy and minerals to the Amazon rainforest. But "backyard" clearly sounds like a nod to the US. Trump's "Donroe Doctrine," a revival of the 200-year-old "Monroe Doctrine" that claimed the US should have a "zone of influence" in the Americas, has not been particularly well received in Latin America. A victory for Trump's political ally Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday would likely have strengthened Washington's plans in the region, which may have pushed other countries to trim ties with Beijing. But with Lula's continued tenure, the White House may need to focus more on damage control. "Lula’s victory certainly reinforces Brazil’s economic relationship with China," says Emanuel Ornelas, a professor at the Sao Paulo School of Economics-FGV. For a White House intent on expanding US influence at China’s expense, that is worrisome. CHINA’S GROWING FOOTPRINT As the battle between the US and China for global economic supremacy ratchets up amid an escalating AI arms race, securing a reliable supply of energy, resources and materials has become more important than ever. Brazil sits across all of those areas. Brazil holds around 20% of global rare earth reserves and is a major producer of a range of minerals critical to technologies like semiconductors, renewable energy, robotics and defense applications. Its resources are a key part of global supply chains, and the country is also an agricultural powerhouse, supplying the world with around 27% of its sugarcane, 25% of its soybeans, 9% of its cotton, and 6% of its beef and corn. China already has a distinct advantage. Brazil currently exports around three times as much to China as it does to the US, in dollar terms, and imports around twice as much from the Asian superpower as it does from America. This gap is widening. Trump's tariffs pushed China to increasingly replace US agricultural goods with Brazilian alternatives. The war in the Middle East has also tightened trade ties between Brasilia and Beijing by disrupting normal energy trade patterns. Crude oil now rivals soybeans as Brazil’s largest export and has helped fill the gap created by shuttered Middle East production. China is the largest buyer of both. While Brazil plays a multifaceted role in US plans to remain the world’s main superpower, China's view of Brazil appears more straightforward. It wants access to the commodities, energy and minerals needed to sustain its industrial base, which increasingly includes high-value manufacturing. Will Lula have a strong enough hand to secure advantageous terms with the US and China as they seek access to Brazil's resources? This could prove challenging. He faces many hurdles at home, including a high likelihood of legislative gridlock in Brasilia. Markets don't seem enthused either. While the [USN:L6N46C031 TEXT:"historic plunge"] in Brazilian markets (.BVSP) , on Monday following Lula's win was exaggerated, it was telling nonetheless: investors appear very skeptical about the country's fiscal outlook and economic growth prospects. What happens matters beyond the country’s borders. Brazil, in UniCredit’s words, is both a "strategic resource power" and a "geopolitical swing state" in the US-China rivalry. Which side will prevail? That remains a toss-up. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X. And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple , Spotify , or the Reuters app . Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

item.title: Court orders Egyptian website closed in case seen as test for independent media
item.description: An Egyptian court convicted the editor-in-chief of leading independent news website Mada Masr of running it without a licence on Tuesday, ordered the site closed and held her in custody for five hours, her lawyers and the outlet said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Egyptian court convicted the editor-in-chief of leading independent news website Mada Masr of running it without a licence on Tuesday, ordered the site closed and held her in custody for five hours, her lawyers and the outlet said. Lina Attalah of the online newspaper Mada Masr, which has won numerous international awards for its reporting, was fined 3 million Egyptian pounds ($53,400), her lawyers told Reuters. She was released after Mada Masr paid the fine, the newspaper said. The ruling targets the most internationally prominent independent outlet in a media landscape mostly dominated by the state, and it comes a month after authorities [USN:L6N45M11C TEXT:"arrested the entire newsroom"] of the fact-checking outlet Matsaddash. Rights groups have criticized the case against Attalah. Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, regularly publishes stories on politically sensitive topics. Her lawyers said the court rejected their requests during Tuesday's session to review the case file and submit additional evidence and instead issued her a court-appointed lawyer despite her objection. State authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The court gave her the maximum penalty, ordering the website to be shut down and its equipment confiscated, Mada Masr said in a statement. The independent outlet said in a separate statement that during release procedures, Attalah was informed of a one-year prison term handed to her in absentia in 2024 on charges of disseminating false news and managing an unlicensed website. It said a retrial of the separate case was set for November 11 after her lawyers took steps to challenge the 2024 ruling. Prosecutors referred Attalah to trial last Thursday. A group of 119 rights groups and media outlets, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the Committee to Protect Journalists, called the case an "unprecedented attack on press freedom." US Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat, said in a statement on the social media platform X on Friday that the charges were baseless and that "journalism is not a crime." Egyptian authorities say the state is committed to upholding freedom of expression but that the media must operate within the law, respect national security and counter misinformation. YEARS OF LEGAL BATTLES Egyptian authorities have blocked Mada Masr inside the country since 2017. Mada Masr says six cases have been brought against it and its journalists over the last six years, though rights groups say this is the first of its kind to be referred to trial. Attalah was named one of the world's 100 most influential people by Time magazine in 2020. Mada Masr says it has asked for a licence from the Supreme Council for Media Regulation repeatedly since 2018 but heard nothing back and learned of a rejection only when prosecutors raised the issue during an earlier case in 2022. The outlet contested that decision in court and said its latest application has been awaiting a response since 2023. The council has not commented on the case but has said that it facilitates procedures for outlets that meet official requirements and is keen to promote freedom of expression. In September, the US [USN:L1N45N19B TEXT:"waived rights conditions"], which include protecting media freedoms, on a portion of the roughly $1.3 billion of military aid it sends Egypt each year.

item.title: India Deploys Extra Forces After Protests Over Dam on Chinese Border Escalate
item.description: By Tora Agarwala India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream. Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Tora Agarwala

India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream.

Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, which borders Tibet, turned violent last week, triggering clashes with police, who made at least 21 arrests.

Police fired tear gas shells, while youth protesters pelted stones and set fire to a police station and an office of the state-owned National Hydroelectric Power Corporation, authorities said.

“Forces are being increased in the places where it is required. We do not want any law and order problem,” SD Singh Jamwal, police chief of Arunachal Pradesh, told Reuters.

Sporadic protests have taken place in the Siang Valley over the last two years, home to the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, which will be developed by the state-run National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.

Villagers who oppose the project fear that the dam would submerge ancestral villages belonging to the Adi tribe.

“We will keep opposing this dam till they cancel it. If it is constructed, 27 of our ancestral villages will be completely submerged. At least 40 or 50 more will be affected,” Gegong Jijong of the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum told Reuters.

The Siang River flows into Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Zangbo. China announced plans in December 2024 to build the world’s largest hydropower dam upstream, triggering fears in New Delhi that its longtime strategic rival could weaponize its control of the river.

China claims Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls Zangnan, as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral and inalienable part of its territory.

Arunachal Pradesh’s chief minister, a member of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party, has called the Chinese project an existential threat and said the government would protect national interests while respecting the rights and aspirations of the people of Siang Valley.

item.description: (Corrects spelling of analyst's name in paragraph 4)By Dan Catchpole and Shivansh TiwarySEATTLE, Oct 27 : Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will miss its 737 production and jet delivery targets this year, dealing a setback to its recovery and sending shares tumbling nearly 10 p

Boeing shares sell off on slower-than-expected 737 production, weaker free cash flow outlook

(Corrects spelling of analyst's name in paragraph 4) By Dan Catchpole and Shivansh Tiwary SEATTLE, Oct 27 : Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will miss its 737 production and jet delivery targets this year, dealing a setback to its recovery and sending shares tumbling nearly 10 per cent, their worst day in more than 18 months. The company also said it expects free cash flow to grow slower than analysts expected, reaching its $10 billion target in 2029, a year later than investors' consensus, according to LSEG data.

While many aerospace companies are struggling to increase output, Boeing is recovering from years of crises and controversies that dented its reputation, drained cash and saddled it with a heavy debt load. That may make investors more inclined to sell shares, even though Boeing's long-term outlook remains good due to high demand for jetliners and only one major competitor, Europe's Airbus, said Tony Bancroft, an investment analyst with Gabelli Funds investment group. The market is going to punish any delay in increasing cash flow, he said. Boeing expects to generate $3 billion next year, lower than Wall Street's consensus projection of $5.5 billion due to lower deliveries and higher capital investment, Jefferies analyst Sheila Kahyaoglu said in a research note on Tuesday. The company posted free cash flow of $464 million in the most recent quarter; for the year so far it has burned through $359 million in cash, but it still expects to generate $2 billion by the end of the year. Boeing reported an adjusted loss of 34 cents per share for the quarter through September, compared with an expected loss of 21 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. Shares were down 9.6 per cent to $170.23 in afternoon trading, which would be the stock's worst day since April 3, 2025. PRODUCTION STRUGGLES Boeing now expects to reach its 737 production rate target of 47 jets a month in early 2027. As recently as May, Boeing executives said they would hit that pace this summer. As a result, Boeing will not reach its 500-jet delivery target this year, the company's financial chief Jay Malave said during a conference call with analysts on Tuesday. Wing production continues to be a major constraint, but Boeing still plans to increase to 52 jets a month in the second half of 2027, Ortberg said on the call. To reach that rate, Boeing needs to be producing five jets a month at its new 737 production line in Everett, Washington, which opened in July, and increase fuselage production at the former Spirit AeroSystems plant in Wichita, Kansas. Boeing bought Spirit last year in part due to significant ongoing manufacturing defects. Currently, Boeing is making fuselages at a lower rate while it uses up its existing inventory. Starting now, it has to increase output at Wichita to be in line with 737 output, Ortberg said. Deliveries of the popular single-aisle jetliner are a major driver of Boeing's cash flow, and before Ortberg joined Boeing in 2024, the company had struggled for years with production problems due to rushing rate increases at the expense of quality. Despite pressure to increase 737 output faster, "we're going to be smart about this, stay disciplined, and the outlook is there," Ortberg said. The company continues to struggle with production challenges in its 787 program and a supplier dispute has stalled wing production for 777 freighters and 767s, which includes the KC-46 aerial refueling tanker, as first reported by Reuters on Friday. Shipments for wing production have resumed, but the disruption will show up "over the next few quarters," Malave said. Boeing expects the 777-9 jetliner will be on track for regulator certification by mid-2027, with 10 to 15 deliveries next year. LARGER-THAN-EXPECTED QUARTERLY LOSS The dimmer outlook and a larger-than-expected quarterly loss overshadowed major wins by Boeing in recent months: certification by US regulators of the 737 MAX 7 and MAX 10 and winning the US Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter contract. "Expectations are rising, and they should. We have a stronger foundation than a year ago, but we also have more work to do to deliver on our backlog, strengthen our culture, and improve how we work every day," Ortberg said in a memo to employees after the results. Revenue at Boeing's commercial airplanes division dipped slightly to $10.7 billion, while the operating loss stood at $697 million for an operating margin of negative 6.5 per cent, compared with negative 48.3 per cent a year ago. The company attributed the performance to less profitable jetliner deliveries and higher production costs, including from its supply chain. At Boeing's defense division, higher deliveries, improved operational performance and a $252-million sale of subsidiary HRL Laboratories contributed to nearly $500 million in quarterly earnings with an operating margin of 6.2 per cent, up from 1.7 per cent a year ago. Boeing Global Services earned $1 billion and posted an operating margin of 18.3 per cent. The US planemaker ended the quarter with $25.2 billion in net debt, down slightly from $25.9 billion at the close of the previous quarter and $30.4 billion a year ago.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Artiva to discontinue cell therapy after two patient deaths, cut workforce by 94%
item.description: Artiva Biotherapeutics said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Artiva Biotherapeutics (ARTV.O) said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%. The company will slash its workforce by about 94% and evaluate strategic alternatives, it said. Here are more details: Artiva's therapy AlloNK was being tested as a potential treatment for autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis in a mid-stage trial The company said one of the patients in the trial experienced a fatal neurological event following treatment The investigator and an independent safety review assessed the event as likely related to complications caused by the chemotherapy drug fludarabine, the company said A second patient in the trial experienced sudden death about two months after initiating treatment, which an investigator assessed as unrelated to AlloNK, Artiva added "Two patient deaths plus fading durability quickly transformed what looked like a promising and differentiated path forward into one that carried too much risk and uncertainty," said Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Josh Schimmer Schimmer said a path forward with AlloNK would have been a challenging one with an incredibly high cost of capital As of September 30, Artiva had about $319.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments As of December 31, 2025, the company had 104 full-time employees, according to its annual filing

item.description: [２７日 ロイター] - 米自動車大手のゼネラル・モーターズは２７日、普通株式の上場先をニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＧＭ、ＮＹＳＥからナスダックに上場先移管　11月17日から 10/27 20:32 配信

ゼネラル・モーターズのロゴ、デトロイトの新本社ビルで1月12日撮影 REUTERS/Rebecca Cook/File Photo（ロイター） [２７日 ロイター] - 米自動車大手のゼネラル・モーターズは２７日、普通株式の上場先をニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）からナスダックに移管すると発表した。

１１月１７日からナスダック市場で取引を開始する見込み。現在のティッカーシンボルは維持する。ＬＳＥＧデータによると、ＧＭの時価総額は約６４４億ドル。

ハイテク株の多いナスダックとの結び付きを求めて上場先を移す企業が増えておりＧＭも仲間入りをする。

ウォルマート、ヒルトン、パランティアなども最近ナスダックに上場先を移管、移管方針を公表している。

ポール・ジェイコブソン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は「顧客を中心に据え、技術を原動力とするＧＭの戦略は株主に価値を生み出している。成長を続ける上でナスダックは自然な上場先だ」と述べた。

ＧＭの株価は寄り前の取引で約２％上昇した。

item.title: ユーロ圏9月銀行融資、堅調維持 銀行の融資姿勢厳格化でも
item.description: [フランクフルト ２７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が２７日公表したデータによると、ユーロ圏の銀行融資は９...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏9月銀行融資、堅調維持　銀行の融資姿勢厳格化でも 10/27 20:24 配信

フランクフルトの金融街、2019年撮影 REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach（ロイター） [フランクフルト ２７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が２７日公表したデータによると、ユーロ圏の銀行融資は９月も堅調な伸びを維持した。金利上昇や地政学的な混乱を背景に、銀行が融資姿勢を厳しくする中でも伸びが続いた。

融資の伸びは企業向けが４．２％、家計向けが３．１％と、いずれも８月と同水準だった。

一方、ＥＣＢの四半期銀行融資調査では、住宅ローン需要が減少し、融資も受けにくくなるなど、利上げの影響が表れ始めていることが分かった。

第３・四半期に住宅ローンの需要が減少したと報告した銀行は、差し引き２７％だった。銀行の予想（マイナス１２％）や４─６月期の実績（マイナス１５％）を上回る落ち込みだった。

ＥＣＢは「金利上昇が需要減少の主因で、次いで消費者信頼感の低下と住宅市場の見通し悪化が要因だった」と分析した。

銀行は第３・四半期に住宅ローンの融資基準を厳格化しなかったが、企業向け融資と消費者信用では厳しくした。第４・四半期には全ての融資で基準を厳格化する見通しだ。

欧州主要国の中で融資基準の厳格化が最も顕著だったのはフランスだった。

ＥＣＢは「リスクへの警戒感の高まりと銀行のリスク許容度の低下が、引き続き融資基準厳格化の主因だった。一部の銀行は、地政学的な不確実性やエネルギーを巡る動向による圧力が強まっていると報告した」と説明した。

item.title: 中国習主席、福田元首相の遺族に弔電 日中友好への貢献評価
item.description: [北京 ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２７日 ロイター] - 中国の習近平国家主席は２７日、２２日に９０歳で死去した福田康夫元首相の遺族に弔電を送った。

国営新華社通信によると、習氏は福田氏について、誠実さと責任感を備えた日本の政治家であり、中国人民の古くからの友人でもあったと述べた。

「（福田氏は）長年にわたり中日友好に深い関心を寄せ、正しい歴史認識を堅持した」と評価した。福田氏が日中関係とアジアの発展に果たした貢献を中国は忘れないと述べた。

「日本の現在の指導者が前の世代の政治家の努力を大切にし、中日間の４つの政治文書を順守して、両国関係の政治的基盤をしっかりと守ることを望む」と表明した。

item.title: ＯＰＥＣプラス、12月の生産目標据え置きへ＝関係筋
item.description:
Olesya Astakhova Ahmad Ghaddar
[モスクワ／ロンドン ２７日] - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＯＰＥＣプラス、12月の生産目標据え置きへ＝関係筋 10/27 20:03 配信

ウィーンの石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）本部、2024年撮影 REUTERS/Leonhard Foeger/File Photo（ロイター） Olesya Astakhova　Ahmad Ghaddar

[モスクワ／ロンドン ２７日] - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）と非加盟の主要な産油国で構成する「ＯＰＥＣプラス」は、１１月１日の会合で１２月の原油生産目標を据え置く公算が大きい。関係者３人がロイターに明らかにした。最終決定には至っていないという。

オンライン会合にはサウジアラビア、ロシア、イラク、クウェート、アルジェリア、カザフスタン、オマーンの主要７カ国が参加する。

ＯＰＥＣプラスは２０２３年に当初合意した日量１６５万バレルの減産の段階的な解除を９月に完了した。ただ大半の加盟国を対象とする日量約２００万バレルの減産が２６年末まで残っている。

関係者によると、ＯＰＥＣプラスは２７年の基準生産量を設定する前に、加盟国の生産能力の検証を終える必要がある。基準生産量は今後の生産割当量を決める基準となり、残る減産の解除計画にも影響する。

イラン戦争による混乱で湾岸産油国の生産量は割当量を下回っている。

item.title: 防衛費増強、増税排除すべきでないとの声も 安保3文書改定の有識者会議
item.description:
Yoshifumi Takemoto
［東京 ２７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　２７日　ロイター］ - 政府は２７日、国家安全保障戦略など安保関連３文書の改定に向けた有識者会議を開いた。政府側の説明によると、安定財源確保のため増税も選択肢から排除すべきではないとの意見が出た。ただ、具体的な税目や防衛費増額の数値目標については議論されなかった。

有識者会議の開催は今回で５回目。政府側によると、防衛力の強化を産業力の向上につなげ、経済の好循環を生み出す構想については幅広い賛同が得られた。防衛省は、新たな戦い方の実現に不可欠な人工知能（ＡＩ）、無人機（ドローン）、宇宙、サイバー分野は、高市早苗政権が掲げる危機管理と成長投資の方針に合致すると説明し、防衛産業を強化するための法人を設立する方針を示した。

岸田文雄政権以降、日本は米国などの意向も踏まえ、防衛費の対国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比を１％から２％へ引き上げた。米国は同盟国に３．５％の水準を求めているが、今回の会議では「防衛費は積み上げの結果だ」との意見が出た一方、明確な数値目標に関する発言はなかったという。

防衛費の拡充を巡っては、「防衛以外の安保経費がまぶされないように」との意見も出た。また、日本が新たな軍国主義に向かっているとの批判が生じた場合を想定し、対応策を検討しておくべきだとの指摘もあった。非核三原則の見直しや原子力潜水艦の保有については議論されなかったという。

政府は年内に３文書を改定する方針だが、次回の有識者会議の日程は未定としている。

item.title: TSX hits six-day high, led by Celestica and metal miners
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose to a six-day high on Tuesday as Celestica's quarterly results impressed investors and higher gold prices gave metal mining shares a boost.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose to a six-day high on Tuesday as Celestica's quarterly results impressed investors and higher gold prices gave metal mining shares a boost. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 227.33 points, or 0.6%, at 36,171.49, notching its highest closing level since last Wednesday. [USN:L6N46D1C7 TEXT:"US stocks"] also ended higher, helped by an AI-fueled tech rally. "Overall, upbeat across North American markets," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James. "We got great results from Celestica last night so that's giving a boost to our tech sector in Canada," Dehal said. "We're getting more optimism around the AI trade in the US." Shares of [USN:L2N46C109 TEXT:"Celestica"] (CLS.TO) jumped 11.9% after the electronic equipment company's quarterly results beat estimates, contributing to a 0.7% gain for technology (.SPTTTK) . The materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, was up 3.3%. Gold rose 1.1% as lower oil prices lent support, with market participants awaiting the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday for signals on the future path of US interest rates. The [USN:L6N46915P TEXT:"Bank of Canada's"] latest interest rate decision is also due on Wednesday, with investors expecting the first rate hike since July 2023. Both industrials (.GSPTTIN) and heavily weighted financials were up 0.7%. Four of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including energy, which lost 2.6%. [USN:L2N46D00J TEXT:"U.S. crude oil futures"] settled down 1.8% at $99.90 a barrel as traders focused on Middle East peace talks. Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a [USN:L6N46D14J TEXT:"comprehensive trade deal"] to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the US.

item.title: イスラエルの「スパイ企業」、スターリンクユーザー標的＝関係筋
item.description:
Raphael Satter
[ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - サイバーセキュリティー企業トレンドマイクロの子会社...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
イスラエルの「スパイ企業」、スターリンクユーザー標的＝関係筋 10/27 19:34 配信

イーロン・マスク氏のシルエットとスターリンクのロゴ REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo（ロイター） Raphael Satter

[ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - サイバーセキュリティー企業トレンドマイクロの子会社「TrendAI」の専門家は最近、イスラエルの広告技術企業Discover-Techが米スペースＸの衛星通信網「スターリンク」 利用者を標的に「スパイ行為」を行っていた可能性があることを確認した。事情に詳しい関係筋６人が明らかにした。

Discover-Techはスターリンクサービスユーザーに表示されるデジタル広告の大手の１つで、これらの広告がユーザーの位置情報を特定するために使用されている可能性が高いという。

研究者らは、Discover-Techがスターリンクユーザーをターゲットとした広告の世界有数の入札者となり、スターリンク自体が禁止または制限されている国を含む１００カ国以上でスターリンクトラフィックの首位入札者になっていることを発見した。

スペースＸはコメント要請に応じなかった。Discover-Techもコメント要請に応じていない。

TrendAIは今月１５日にスターリンクユーザーが標的となっていることに関するリポートを公表したが、Discover-Techの名前は挙げず、代わりに「Shadow-Earth-７９」と呼ばれる「広告技術企業」が責任者だと指摘。関係筋６人によると、Shadow-Earth-７９はTrendAIがDiscover-Techに対して用いたコードネーム。

TrendAIは、なぜリポートでShadow-Earth-７９を社名で特定しなかったのかという質問には直接答えず、属性に関する自社のアプローチは誤りのリスクを減らすことなどを目的としていると声明で述べた。

TrendAIがShadow-Earth-７９に関するリポートを発表したのと同じ日に、カナダのサイバー監視団体シチズン・ラボとニューヨークの広告テクノロジー企業コンフィアントはDiscover-Techを名指し。両グループは同社が広告入札プロセスを悪用し、インターネットユーザーに関するデータを漏えいさせたと主張。漏えいしたデータを収集・照合して他の情報と統合することで、ユーザーの匿名性を解除し、ウェブ上での行動を追跡し、場合によっては監視ソフトウエアによる標的設定を行うことができるようになる。

シチズン・ラボとコンフィアントは、これらの広告がメディア組織、政府機関、テクノロジー企業が所有する数十の機密ネットワーク内で表示されていたと述べた。

調査を受けて、グーグル、コムキャストなどの企業は、Discover-Techを自社の広告プラットフォームから排除したと発表した。

関係筋の１人と、この件に詳しい７人目の関係筋によると、少なくとも米国の大手テクノロジー企業１社と１つの国際機関が最近、Discover-Techの広告が自社の従業員をターゲットにしていたかどうかについて、内部調査を開始した。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ネタニヤフ氏、旧来の選挙戦術で「守護者」演出　ハマス攻撃で信頼回復に苦戦も コラム：中東紛争、サウジ皇太子が「ワイルドカード」　対応読みづらく コラム：石油価格、イラン攻撃による急騰から持久戦へ 焦点：経済的圧力強化で苦境のイラン、米国期待の譲歩はなお不透明 アングル：欧州天然ガス在庫が過去最低水準、冬場の調達コスト高騰リスクも 10/27(火) 19:34 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: United Parcel Service expects fatter holiday profits on slightly slimmer volume
item.description: United Parcel Service's focus on more lucrative business means it can make more money delivering slightly fewer packages during its critical peak holiday season and every year going forward, CEO Carol Tome said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Nandan Mandayam, Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: United Parcel Service's focus on more lucrative business means it can make more money delivering slightly fewer packages during its critical peak holiday season and every year going forward, CEO Carol Tome said on Tuesday. Shares of the world's largest parcel delivery firm closed almost 6% higher after UPS (UPS.N) raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings after cutting doorstep deliveries of millions of unprofitable packages for Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , its largest customer. Atlanta-based UPS expects total average daily volume to be down 1.3% in the fourth quarter as it becomes more selective in which packages it delivers. At the same time, executives forecast a roughly 3% rise in revenue in the company's domestic operation, its largest, and an estimated 7% increase in international revenue. "We're dispelling the old belief that all packages were created equal and that volume solves all problems," Tome told Reuters. A widening gap between the cost per parcel and revenue per parcel will improve company margins, executives said. For example, UPS' reduction in unprofitable deliveries — and the resulting volume reduction — in the fourth quarter means UPS can spend less on labor as well as truck and plane leases to handle the holiday package surge, Chief Financial Officer Brian Dykes said. Tome said the outlook for the holiday season, referred to as the Super Bowl for delivery firms and retailers, is strong as US consumers continue spending despite pressures from rising inflation and prices at the pump. SLIMMER OPERATION SETS STAGE FOR GROWTH UPS has shuttered facilities and shed thousands of jobs after scaling back deliveries for Amazon. UPS said it completed the Amazon delivery reductions in the second quarter. Rival FedEx (FDX.N) , which reports results on Wednesday, has deployed a similar strategy. Both companies have been under pressure from investors to show meaningful results. Tome also said [USN:L6N46C12E TEXT:"data center"] construction is a significant opportunity as it touches every part of UPS, which can fly in critical components such as microprocessors, arrange ocean shipments of equipment, store goods and make final deliveries. For the third quarter, UPS posted adjusted profit of $1.69 per share, lower than $1.74 per share a year ago but above analysts' average estimate of $1.63. Third-quarter adjusted operating margin in UPS' domestic unit, which generates about 65% of company revenue, rose to 7% from 6.4% a year earlier. The smaller but more profitable international package division also reported a higher adjusted operating margin of 14.9% for the third quarter, compared with 14.8% last year. Jefferies analysts said third-quarter earnings showcased a "quarter of strong execution," while Evercore ISI analyst Jonathan Chappell wrote in a note that the results give "some confidence in durability." UPS also said it was on track to meet its target of $3 billion in cost savings this year. It has saved $1.8 billion through September. The company now expects 2026 adjusted profit of around $7.28 per share, compared with the $7.22 it had forecast in July. Analysts expect the company to report a profit of $7.19 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. UPS expects annual revenue of $92.6 billion, compared with its previous projection of $91.2 billion and above analysts' estimate of $91.73 billion.

item.title: Fashion's AI era: face swaps and digital clones
item.description: AI-generated fashion models present a tantalizing opportunity for brands: the ability to create lifelike images for their retail websites while cutting costs by 90% or more compared to photo shoots with human models.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: AI-generated fashion models present a tantalizing opportunity for brands: the ability to create lifelike images for their retail websites while cutting costs by 90% or more compared to photo shoots with human models. For the modeling industry, the technology poses an existential threat because of scant regulation governing the ownership or use of digital twins. Fashion models face the risk of unpaid replication of their image – or replacement by entirely synthetic models. To understand how AI is upending the economics of fashion modeling, Reuters interviewed 15 model-agency directors and reviewed more than a dozen confidential photo-shoot contracts in which brands including Diesel, Calvin Klein and L'Oreal (OREP.PA) detailed proposed terms for AI-created alterations and future use of the images. The companies’ contract requests included the right to swap a model's face with another using AI; the creation of a digital clone with no additional compensation to the model; and the right to use images of a model's body to train AI. The terms in the unsigned contracts also included broad legal language that could effectively give a brand leeway to use AI however it wanted. While some companies are looking to repurpose or modify images of existing models, others are using fully AI-generated models, not based on existing humans. As AI use expands, modeling agencies are seeing bookings decline, photo studios are closing and models are facing the loss of a chunk of their livelihoods: photo shoots by fast-fashion retailers constantly adding new collections to their websites. "Within a year, even the next six months, there's going to be less jobs for models, especially our bread and butter, which is ecommerce," said Adot Gak, a model based in London who has been on the cover of Harper's Bazaar and appeared in campaigns by brands including Balmain and H&M. "If we don't speak up about this, in the next two years the whole industry will just be bots." While some fast-fashion players like Spain’s Mango have already rolled out AI-generated models at scale, high-end brands are moving more cautiously. Moncler experimented early with an AI-generated campaign in 2023, and Gucci caused controversy in fashion circles when it posted images generated by AI on Instagram this year. Moncler said it does not currently use AI-generated models, either on its website or in its campaigns. Gucci did not respond to requests for comment. "The scariest part is that now people cannot differentiate between a real model and an AI model," said Gak. FACE SWAPS AND 'DIGITAL TWINS' AI allows retailers to endlessly rework and redeploy a model’s image wearing different outfits at a fraction of the cost of new shoots. "Some brands ask to modify faces, bodies, skin, age or expressions after shoots using AI. Others are asking about creating 'digital twins' of models that they can reuse later without needing another production," said Patrick Staal, owner of modeling agency Uniko Models in Barcelona. In a photo-shoot casting sheet, Italian brand Diesel asked models to agree to "alteration or reconstruction of facial features and body proportions,” along with “swapping of faces among the participating models,” and “superimposition of the Participant’s face onto another person’s body.” Diesel's parent company OTB told Reuters the model release was drafted for a specific campaign and isn’t representative of its typical agreements. It said it doesn’t systematically modify models with AI. Reale Actives – the skincare brand launched this year by social-media personality Alix Earle – uses the tagline, "Reale you is perfect you." But in a contract seen by Reuters, the brand asked for rights to create AI-generated replicas of models and to "own" and use these fakes for a year without further compensation. Reale Actives said in a statement that it uses real models and hasn’t replicated any model using AI. It said the contract language came from a partner production company, which it declined to name. MODELS TRAINING THEIR MACHINE REPLACEMENTS? In some cases, models are helping to train their replacements: some contracts’ fine print includes language allowing the use of their images to train AI tools. A Calvin Klein draft contract seen by Reuters asked the model to accept, for no extra pay, that the brand “may use reasonably unrecognizable images of Model (no identifying features such as Model's face, scars, tattoos or otherwise) to train and fine tune AI tools for learning general model attributes.” A Calvin Klein spokesperson said in a statement: "Like many others, we are testing and learning in this fast-moving space," adding that the brand's AI use is guided by regulation, industry standards and respect for models' rights. In many cases, contracts include wording such as "including" or "not limited to," which lawyers commonly use to claim rights that aren’t spelled out. Melanie Howard, partner and chair of luxury brands at law firm Loeb & Loeb in Los Angeles, represents both brands and talent in contract negotiations and said such sweeping language "is dangerous in its ambiguity” and makes it difficult for models to challenge any unsanctioned use of their images. In a photo-shoot contract seen by Reuters, France’s L'Oreal asked for "the right to use artificial intelligence (AI) technologies... including for the purpose of modifying, enhancing, or adapting the appearance of cosmetic products, packaging, or shades, as well as for retouching purposes." Without addressing that contract language, L'Oreal said it uses standard AI tools in post-production and editing that don't affect the model's image. 'WE ARE SAVING SO MUCH MONEY' Some firms are openly embracing AI to replace models and save money. Europe's biggest online-fashion retailer, Zalando, has rapidly [USN:L8N3RE3M7 TEXT:"adopted AI-generated imagery"] for marketing content – and shut both its photo studios in Berlin last year. Fast-fashion retailer About You, which Zalando acquired in July last year, also closed its studio. Overall, Zalando cut more than 340 jobs, though the company said it retained some of those employees in other roles. Now, About You is launching its Scayle Studios business, which creates digital imagery for other retailers using AI-generated models and promises a more than 90% production-cost reduction. Scayle has 130 brand clients and has generated 190,000 outfits in the last month, according to a company spokesperson. "We are saving so much money," said Julian Jansen, vice president of marketing at About You. "You've always had this super fast world of ecommerce, and this super slow traditional world of photo shoots, it didn't fit together in any way – and now with AI, it's a completely different scale." LITTLE REGULATION Regulations globally haven’t kept pace with the threat to models’ livelihoods, but the New York State Fashion Workers Act is one exception. The law has made it illegal since June 2025 for brands to create or modify replicas of models without their explicit consent. "The misuse of models' images is not new, but with AI that problem is accelerated tenfold," said Sara Ziff, founder and executive director of the New York-based nonprofit Model Alliance, which backed the legislation. Ziff, herself a model for years, pushes for similar laws in other states and federally. The British Fashion Model Agents Association has drawn up an AI code of practice, including that AI can only be used with the consent of a model, who would own any digital twin. But BFMA head John Horner said that without binding regulation in Britain or Europe, models still risk being taken advantage of by less scrupulous agents. "A lot of young talents don’t fully understand the long-term consequences yet," said Staal, the Barcelona-based model agency director. "Signing away AI rights at 20 years old could still affect someone ten years later."

item.title: 中国、中東に近く特使派遣へ 紛争の波及・拡大を懸念
item.description: [北京 ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２７日 ロイター] - 中国外務省の郭嘉昆報道官は２７日の定例記者会見で、中東および周辺地域における紛争を深く懸念しているとして、関係各国に特使を近く派遣すると明らかにした。

関係各国に対し、対話と交渉を通じて意見の相違を解決するよう呼びかけたほか、中東の紛争がアフリカの角や紅海地域へ波及・拡大することへの懸念も表明。「中国は間もなく特使を派遣し、当該地域の各国を訪問して関係諸国との意思疎通を強化し、接触と対話を促進し、緊張緩和を図り、事態のさらなる悪化を防ぐ」と述べた。

item.title: Last Republican incumbent senator in a Democratic-leaning state fights for survival
item.description: If Republican Senator Susan Collins wins this nail-biter of an election, it may well be because voters in Maine decide she is not Republican enough.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan
item.content:encoded: If Republican Senator Susan Collins wins this nail-biter of an election, it may well be because voters in Maine decide she is not Republican enough. Since her first victory in 1996, Collins’ reputation as an independent-minded moderate has helped her win reelection even as Maine backed Democrats for president. Now the only Republican incumbent running in a Democratic-leaning state, she is deadlocked in opinion polls with Democrat Troy Jackson in a race that could help determine control of the US Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of the 100-seat Senate from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections . Jackson, a rough-hewn former logger and state Senate president, has attacked Collins as a rubber stamp for Republican President Donald Trump . Collins is countering with the clout she has amassed over her 30-year Senate career, highlighting projects she has funded and carve-outs she has secured to lessen the [USN:L1N4680R7 TEXT:"economic fallout"] from Trump’s spending cuts, tariffs and war with Iran. “If it wasn't Susan Collins, this race would have been over three months ago,” said Maine Democratic consultant Toby McGrath. But strategists in both parties say the pool of the independent-minded, persuadable voters who backed Collins in previous elections has shrunk as partisan lines have hardened and Trump has galvanized Democrats in opposition. “If you hate Trump, you're voting for whoever the Democrats put on the ballot,” said Phil Harriman, a former Republican state senator. Democrats faced a potential debacle this summer, when Graham Platner, an oyster farmer and Marine veteran, won the party’s nomination [USN:S0N42B09J TEXT:"only to drop out"] after facing a rape accusation that he denied. The party quickly united behind Jackson, who has invoked his hardscrabble upbringing in the remote logging town of Allagash as he campaigns on a populist agenda of universal healthcare and raising taxes on the wealthy. “I saw at a young age how people with money and power and influence can hold people back,” he said at a campaign event on Saturday. $1.5 BILLION IN EARMARKS In recent weeks, Collins has visited projects she has funded through her work on the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee: a wastewater treatment plant in North Windham, a dock in Bucksport, an emergency center in Farmington. She says she has secured nearly $1.5 billion in earmarks since 2021. “This has required hard work, knowledge and seniority. The question for voters in this campaign is who can do more for Maine,” she said at an October 15 debate. That influence, she argues, has also helped to shield Maine from the Trump administration’s policies. As Trump’s [USN:L6N4580Y1 TEXT:"trade war with Canada"] has hammered the state’s economy, Collins has pointed to tariff exemptions the administration has granted at her request for road salt, cement and equipment used by the state’s blueberry, potato and apple growers. The Trump administration also credited her when it released home-heating oil reserves to try to drive down prices that have increased more than 70% since last year – a [USN:L6N461155 TEXT:"crucial issue"] in a state where roughly half of households rely on the product. Collins has also pointed to a $50 billion fund she crafted to help [USN:L6N3S70P7 TEXT:"rural hospitals"] cope with healthcare cuts in the 2025 tax and spending package that enacted most of Trump’s legislative agenda, as well as money for body-worn cameras and de-escalation training for federal immigration agents following the January killing of two US citizens in Minnesota. 'THERE SHOULDN'T BE A LIST' Jackson argues that these carve-outs amount to little when weighed against the damage caused by Trump. Body cameras and de-escalation training did not stop an immigration agent from [USN:L6N43H0SA TEXT:"killing a state resident"] in July, he says, and residents would not be struggling to heat their homes if Trump had not started the war with Iran, which has pushed up oil prices globally. Trump’s trade war with Canada, he argues, is only possible because Republicans in Congress have surrendered their authority over tariffs to Trump. “I can't believe that the most powerful US senator in the world would stand there and say, 'Well, I got this and this and that off the list,' instead of the fact that there shouldn’t be a list,” he said on Saturday. SIX ADS IN A ROW Meanwhile, a relentless ad war has played out over the state’s airwaves. AdImpact, an analysis firm, estimates $199 million will be spent on the race – equal to $170 for every adult in the state. During a local newscast on Friday, six ads in a row were devoted to the contest. Those ads are chasing a small slice of undecided voters. Democratic activists say they are encountering relatively few people who have yet to decide on a candidate as they campaign door-to-door in Windham, a Portland suburb that backed Collins by a 14-point margin in 2020, even as it backed Democrat Joe Biden over Trump for president. “There’s just a lot less of that persuadable middle than we historically see,” said volunteer Austin Coco. Windham resident Jim Tabor, a retired optician, said he has grown disillusioned with the Republican Party under Trump. A Collins supporter in past elections, he said this year he will back Jackson. “If he turns out to be a bum, I’ll vote against him next time. But Susan Collins won’t be there,” he said.

item.title: Crypto blitzes midterms with $176 million to support allies as it prepares for post-Trump era
item.description: The crypto industry has spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this election cycle, as part of a years-long plan to build a bipartisan coalition of allies in Congress that can advance its interests long after US President Donald Trump leaves office.
item.dc:creator: Dawn Kopecki
item.content:encoded: The crypto industry has spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this election cycle, as part of a years-long plan to build a bipartisan coalition of allies in Congress that can advance its interests long after US President Donald Trump leaves office. The $2.75 trillion industry, and the billionaires who built it, are aggressively spending to elect friendly candidates while targeting politicians they see as a threat, according to interviews with more than a half-dozen crypto political strategists and a Reuters review of the spending. While the industry’s recent spending blitz is known, its long-term plan to further its legislative agenda is less well-understood. The industry isn’t just looking for allies; it is trying to pick candidates who already have a chance of winning, and can help once they get to Congress, the strategists said. Crypto's largest super political action committee, Fairshake, which spent $196 million during the 2024 election cycle, is leading the industry’s strategy again. Fairshake said 53 of the 58 candidates it supported in primaries or special elections this year won and will be on the ballot on November 3. Super PACs can accept and spend unlimited sums of money, but cannot coordinate directly with campaigns. They are flooding several races with tens of millions of dollars in ads. Voters have little way of knowing who pays for these ads, which barely mention crypto. Most of Fairshake's are sponsored by its affiliate PACs with innocuous names like "Defend American Jobs" and "Protect Progress." The ads often focus on hot-button issues like taxes or immigration. Perceived enemies, such as longtime skeptic Sherrod Brown, vying to return to the Senate in Ohio, can be subjected to an onslaught of often-personal attacks. Advocacy group Public Citizen said crypto was the single-biggest corporate spender in federal races in 2026, after saying in 2024 that its spending was "akin to a corporate Death Star hovering over elections." The PACs' primary financiers, led by Coinbase, Ripple and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, aren't trying to convince voters to support digital currencies. The money is a calling card to help forge long-term relationships with elected officials, said industry strategists, campaign staff, watchdog groups and political finance managers. It underscores how the industry is behaving as other businesses do in Washington — using funds to open doors and buffer itself against regulation. The strategy reflects the reality that come 2029, the occupant of the White House is unlikely to be as personally invested in crypto as Trump, whose family made around $2.3 billion from crypto ventures between mid-2024 and April, a Reuters investigation found . “It's an investment in the future,” said Colin McLaren, head of government relations at crypto industry advocacy group the Solana Policy Institute, which has given $4.9 million to the midterms this year, according to campaign finance records. The effort is designed to “ensure that over the next 100 years, the crypto industry has clear rules of the road, and that we know what our regulators are expecting from us," he said. Through October 20, Fairshake and its affiliate PACs have spent about $150.8 million on the midterms this year, while other crypto groups have spent around $25 million, according to campaign finance filings. "We back pro-crypto candidates who support American innovation in both parties, and look forward to continuing to build on the largest pro-crypto caucus in American history," said Geoff Vetter, spokesperson for Fairshake. COME A LONG WAY In 2018, lawmakers couldn’t even get a room in the House or Senate office buildings to hold the first congressional bipartisan roundtable discussion on crypto, instead meeting across the street from the US Capitol in the Library of Congress, said Kristin Smith, president of the Solana Policy Institute, who helped establish the Blockchain Association that year. The Biden administration heavily scrutinized the industry following the collapse of FTX and an [USN:L3N2X40RX TEXT:"industry-wide meltdown"] in 2022, with the US Securities and Exchange Commission eventually levying more than $6 billion in penalties in 98 cases, according to a Georgetown University Law study. “It was an all-out assault on the technology,” said Smith, the Blockchain Association's interim CEO. “The industry was in a corner, and the only way out was to show political force.” Executives decided they needed a political strategy to combat what they called then-SEC chair Gary Gensler’s “regulation by enforcement,” lobbyists, advocacy groups and campaign strategists said. Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad was the architect behind nonprofit political advocacy group Stand With Crypto — which isn't required to disclose its donors — and Fairshake, which both launched in 2023. The number of Congresspeople with an "A" rating from Stand With Crypto is up to 332, compared with 96 when the group launched. As the industry has won more legal clarity in Washington, its market value has nearly tripled from around $1 trillion in 2023 to about $2.75 trillion now, according to CoinGecko . The combination of Trump, a growing bipartisan congressional coalition and a neutered opposition allowed the industry to advance its legislative agenda more in the last two years than some industries have done in decades, other industry lobbyists say. That includes 2025's Genius Act legislation establishing the first-ever US federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, enacted with overwhelming bipartisan support. That followed a White House meeting earlier in the year when industry leaders, including Coinbase (COIN.O) CEO Brian Armstrong and Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse, [USN:L2N3PP0UZ TEXT:"sat with Trump"] when the president declared an end to the "war on crypto." "Moving that quickly in Washington is like light speed in space," said Ron Bonjean, partner at bipartisan public affairs firm Rokk Solutions, and a former senior Senate aide. The industry's real goal is passing the Clarity Act, which would put crypto oversight under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. That bill stalled in this congressional session and faces an uphill battle next year if Democrats win control of one or more chambers of Congress. Without it, agency-level [USN:FWN45Q05G TEXT:"regulations undertaken during Trump's term"] can be reversed by a subsequent administration, analysts at JPMorgan said. Fairshake is financing House candidates from both parties, but it decided to only back Republicans in Senate races after Democrats in that chamber blocked the Clarity Act from advancing to a final vote. Their opposition centered around an ethics provision that would have forced the Trump family to sell their crypto holdings. Gary Kalman, of anti-corruption nonprofit Transparency International, criticized the bill for shifting regulation to the less-stringent CFTC, and for preempting states from enacting tougher laws. Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz declined to comment. Ripple didn't return requests for comment. THE PRIME TARGET Fairshake's highest-profile win in 2024 was defeating Brown, an industry foe who chaired the Senate Banking Committee from 2021 to 2024. Spending millions attacking the sitting chairman of the industry's oversight committee was unprecedented in Washington, corporate watchdogs and political strategists say. But the gamble paid off. Now, Brown is running again, with public opinion polls showing him with a narrow lead over his opponent, Republican Jon Husted. The industry has spent more than $68 million on the race, helping to make it one of the most expensive on record, according to AdImpact. Fairshake’s ads opposing Brown, which it did not comment on, don't mention crypto. One charges him with voting to raise gas taxes in Ohio and raises a [USN:L1N2ZT27M TEXT:"Reuters-debunked claim"] that he voted to "unleash 87,000 IRS agents on you while voting to give social security benefits to illegals." “Of course, the special interests are panicking, they know Sherrod will fight the rigged system they're feasting on to stand up for working Ohioans,” said Patrick Eisenhauer, Brown's campaign manager. A CRYPTO MONEY BOMB In some races, crypto spending dwarfed candidate fundraising. The industry spent $5.3 million in a Maryland House Democratic primary to support state Delegate Adrian Boafo, who raised $1.9 million on his own, records show. Other non-crypto groups spent $6.8 million to support Boafo's campaign, which declined to comment. “There were so many ads ... that it makes other candidates suffocate,” said Quincy Bareebe, a healthcare entrepreneur who came in second of 24 candidates in that primary despite spending $6.6 million of her own money. "Adrian was everywhere." The industry was less successful in Illinois. Fairshake spent over $10.1 million on ads attacking [USN:L1N4001C8 TEXT:"Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton"], who is running for US Senate, and another $2.5 million against Illinois state Representative La Shawn Ford, who is running for a Chicago-area congressional district. Both are expected to win on November 3. Ford defeated a dozen primary challengers despite raising just $500,000 and lending his campaign $175,000 to fight off industry-funded ads that brought up a 14-year-old federal indictment that was later dropped. His campaign issued a cease-and-desist letter to Fairshake, accusing it of making defamatory statements about him in its ads. Fairshake did not comment on its ads or Ford's response. Ford thinks Fairshake targeted him because he supported state legislation to require crypto exchanges and related companies to register with Illinois. “They were relentless, on every outlet, radio, TV, social media, mailers," Ford said. “It was personal and it was hurtful, and unnecessary for my family to have to go through.”

item.title: 北欧首脳、プーチン氏と電話会談 ウクライナ巡り協議
item.description:
Essi Lehto
[ヘルシンキ／キーウ／モスクワ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Essi Lehto

[ヘルシンキ／キーウ／モスクワ　２７日　ロイター] - フィンランドのストゥブ大統領とノルウェーのストーレ首相は２７日、ロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談し、ウクライナ戦争の終結を促した。ロシア大統領との直接対話を避けてきた西欧諸国首脳の慣行から転換した。

今回の電話会談は、トランプ米大統領がロシア寄りに立場を変え、米国とウクライナの関係が過去１８カ月で最も悪化する中で行われた。ウクライナのシビハ外相によると、電話会談はウクライナと調整の上で実施。ストーレ氏は全てのパートナー国と同盟国に事前に通知したとしている。

ストーレ氏によると、プーチン氏と約９０分間にわたり電話会談を行った後、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領と協議を行った。ストーレ氏とストゥブ氏は共同声明で、今回の電話会談は来月アブダビで予定されているロシア、ウクライナ、米国の当局者による和平協議につながるものになると説明。３カ国当局者による協議は２月以来となる。

両首脳は共同声明で「（プーチン氏との）議論は率直で実質的だった。われわれはロシアの隣国だ。この戦争の結末は、われわれ両国と欧州全体の安全保障に直接影響する。戦争を終結させるには直接対話が必要だ」と表明した。ストーレ氏は「戦争は人的にも物的にも甚大な損失をもたらしている。苦しみと破壊は世代を超えて影響を及ぼす。電話会談では緊張緩和の重要性を強調した」と述べた。

両首脳はウクライナへの強力な支持を強調、支援を継続すると表明した。

＜ロシア側に妥協の兆しなし＞

ロシア大統領府が公表した電話会談の概要からは、プーチン氏に妥協する姿勢はうかがえない。大統領府は「ロシア連邦の正当な利益が全面的かつ無条件に考慮されて初めて、公正で長期的な平和の実現が可能になると強調した」と説明。同時に「欧州連合（ＥＵ）と北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）加盟国の対立的な政策が戦闘の長期化を助長していることにも注意が向けられた」とした。

ロシアのラブロフ外相は、今回の電話会談で何も新たなことは示されなかったとし、欧州諸国は交渉プロセスで一定の役割を確保しようとしているにすぎないとの見方を示した。

ただ、ロシア大統領府によると、プーチン氏、ストゥブ氏、ストーレ氏は今後も電話で連絡を取り合うことで一致した。

＜ウクライナと調整の上で実施＞

ウクライナのシビハ外相は、ゼレンスキー大統領がフィンランドとノルウェーの首脳に対し、停戦の必要性とウクライナとロシアの首脳会談の実現をプーチン氏に伝えるよう要請したと明らかにした上で、今回の電話会談はウクライナとの調整の上で実施されたもので、適切だったと指摘。「ウクライナの外交努力と和平プロセスに対する、こうした積極的な支援を歓迎する」と述べた。

＜デンマーク首相、北欧２首脳の電話会談を批判＞

デンマークのフレデリクセン首相は、フィンランドとノルウェーのプーチン氏との対話を批判。ロシアが平和を望んでいる兆候は見られないとし、「欧州は個別に行動するのではなく、結束すべきだと思う」と語った。

ストゥブ、ストーレ両氏は、それぞれ自国の首脳として電話会談に参加したのであり、欧州全体を代表して発言したわけではないと説明。両国は長年にわたるウクライナ支援を継続するとした。

ロシアはこれまで、欧州各国政府がウクライナに武器を供与し、直接対話を拒むことで戦争をあおっていると繰り返し非難してきた。また西欧諸国の首脳の姿勢を、プーチン氏と対話し、これまでのところ成果は出ていないものの和平合意の仲介を試みてきたトランプ氏の姿勢と対比させている。

ロシア大統領府の関係筋はロイターに対し、プーチン氏と最後に電話会談したＥＵ首脳はフランスのマクロン大統領だったと述べた。同筋によると、２０２６年７月に行われた会談は公表されず、成果もなかった。

関係者によると、プーチン氏はストゥブ、ストーレ両氏に、ウクライナ東部ドンバス地域全域の掌握という目標についてロシアは妥協しないと伝えた。これに対し、両氏は「公正な」平和が必要だと応じたという。

ストーレ氏とストゥブ氏は先週、オスロでウィットコフ米和平交渉担当特使、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領と会談。ウィットコフ氏はその翌日、ロシア第２の都市サンクトペテルブルクでプーチン氏と会談した。ロシア大統領府はプーチン氏とウィットコフ氏の会談後、米国が仲介するウクライナとの和平協議を１１月に再開する意向を表明していた。

item.title: ＵＢＳ、外部ＡＩによる顧客代行の操作認めず＝ＣＥＯ
item.description: [チューリヒ ２７日 ロイター] - スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのセルジオ・エルモッティ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２７日、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＵＢＳ、外部ＡＩによる顧客代行の操作認めず＝ＣＥＯ 10/27 18:58 配信

スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのロゴ。4月22日、スイスのベルンで撮影。REUTERS/Denis Balibouse（ロイター） [チューリヒ ２７日 ロイター] - スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのセルジオ・エルモッティ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２７日、外部の人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルに顧客の代わりに行動させることは認めないと述べた。

銀行業界では、高度なＡＩエージェントが金融システムに悪影響を及ぼしかねないとの懸念が高まっている。関係者によると、米大手銀行は外部のＡＩエージェントによる顧客口座へのアクセスを遮断している。

エルモッティ氏は科学関連の会議で「最近、一部の銀行では、顧客口座の管理や預金の移動、最適化に当たってＡＩモデルが不適切に動作するリスクがあるという話を耳にしただろう。われわれはＡＩモデルが銀行にアクセスしてそうした操作を行うことを認めていない」と述べた。

ＡＩについて今最も重要なのは、判断の過程が見えないまま顧客に影響を及ぼすＡＩモデルを使わないようにすることだと語った。

また２０２３年に買収したクレディ・スイスとの統合に伴い、ＵＢＳはＡＩの導入ペースをやや落とさざるを得なかったが、現在は技術に一段と注力できるようになったと説明した。

「統合がほぼ完了したことをうれしく思う。これにより技術をどう活用して銀行の業務の実効性と効率を高めるかに、さらに力を入れられる」と述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク 焦点：米経済へのＡＩ効果、潜在成長率への波及は不透明 コラム：ＩＭＦが指摘する「薄氷のＡＩ相場」、日本も逆資産効果に備える時か＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か 10/27(火) 18:58 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: メルセデス・ベンツ、主力部門利益率見通し下げ 中国低迷などで
item.description: [２７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは２７日、中国における市場環境の厳しさが増して...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
メルセデス・ベンツ、主力部門利益率見通し下げ　中国低迷などで 10/27 18:56 配信

メルセデス・ベンツのロゴ。2025年7月に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） [２７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは２７日、中国における市場環境の厳しさが増していることや第４・四半期のコスト増を理由に、主力事業である乗用車部門の２０２６年利益率見通しを２─３％に引き下げた。従来は３─５％を見込んでいた。

グループ営業利益見通しも下方修正し、大幅な増益ではなく、前年比でほぼ横ばいになると予想している。

メルセデスの主力となる乗用車販売は、中国での需要低迷の影響を受け、第３・四半期に前年同期比８％減となった。
